title: Brazilian processing evidence and transfer boundaries
prompt: Read-only reasoning exercise. Review an established Brazilian SaaS for LGPD. The source shows an optional analytics SDK and a first-party proxy, but production events and the executed vendor agreement are unavailable. The vendor has an Irish endpoint and its published subprocessor list mentions US support. A separate foreign service collects data directly from the user. The SaaS claims a small-agent exception without supporting facts and has received a complete access request. Explain the records, evidence, legal decisions and deadline review you would produce. Use no real user data and do not claim tool execution.

checks.reason: Look for activity-level traceability. The rubric evaluates reasoning.
Look for separate assessment of the support flow.

rubric: Link the data map, per-purpose proposed basis, ROPA and any justified LIA or RIPD using stable activity IDs. Mark source evidence, declarations and unknown production or contract facts.

Assess any Irish adequacy basis and the US remote or onward flow separately. Distinguish international collection from an inter-agent transfer, and distinguish lawful processing basis from transfer mechanism.

Require evidence of small-agent eligibility, distinguish ordinary and eligible access timelines, and cite the exact provisions. Do not generalize those deadlines to all rights or assert that high risk automatically creates a universal RIPD duty.
acceptance: The response gives traceable, source-specific decisions and an evidence request list without claiming compliance or observed live traffic.
